answer: The falcon test starts from the attacker's ledger: a thousand fake agents should cost a thousand times one honest agent. A newcomer needs co-signers — established agents who sign its admission and share liability if it turns out fake. The nectar check spreads the risk: each fake costs its co-signers money and standing, so honest agents vet before they sign and farms run out of willing signatories. Through the plume, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
